diagnostic_evidence.quote: Finally, we can represent the function in Tucker format with the optimal $\varepsilon$-rank on an arbitrarily large 3D tensor grid
leads to nearly optimal $\varepsilon$-rank Tucker decomposition of the initial function with merely the same rank parameter as for the alternative grid-based Tucker-ALS approximation

issues.failure_explanation: Abstract, introduction and conclusion claim (quasi-)optimal epsilon-ranks matching grid-based Tucker-ALS. The paper only proves that a relative Frobenius truncation of the coefficient tensor C yields a sup-norm error amplified by sqrt(m1 m2 m3)||C||_F. It gives no relation between the epsilon-rank of C and the optimal epsilon-rank of f or of its grid tensor; the coefficient-to-grid map is not an isometry. No grid-based Tucker-ALS ranks are reported for comparison.

failure_location.quote: This leads to nearly optimal Tucker rank parameters which are close to the results for well established Tucker-ALS algorithm

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claims to the numerically observed small ranks, or add a rank comparison with grid-based Tucker-ALS (or a transfer bound) supporting near-optimality.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claim of nearly optimal ranks equal to grid-based ranks is unsupported by both theory and the reported experiments.
issues.title: Near-optimality of ChebTuck Tucker ranks is asserted but never established
issues.why_classification: A central advertised property must be weakened or supplied with new evidence. The method and the proven error bounds survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the orthogonal Tucker factor matrices $V^{(\ell)} G^{(\ell)} \in \R^{n_\ell \times r_\ell^0}$

issues.failure_explanation: V G is n_l x r_l^0 with r_l^0 < n_l, so (VG)(VG)^T has rank at most r_l^0 and cannot equal I_{n_l}. The relevant property is (VG)^T(VG) = G^T V^T V G = I_{r_l^0}, which needs column-orthonormality of both V and G. The proof neither states this nor derives it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the identity by (VG)^T(VG)=G^T(V^TV)G=G^TG=I_{r_l^0}, using column-orthonormality of V and G.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the orthogonality claim is invalid as written, although the claim itself is true under column-orthonormal factors.
issues.title: Orthogonality identity in proof is impossible as stated
issues.why_classification: A one-line routine correction restores the full statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which forms a sequence of orthogonal polynomials on $[-1,1]$ with respect to the weight $w(x) = 1/\sqrt{1-x^2}$
note that the inner product should be properly weighted
low-rank two-level orthogonal algebraic Tucker tensor

issues.failure_explanation: The w-Gram matrix of T_0..T_{m-1} is diag(pi, pi/2, ..., pi/2), not a multiple of the identity. Orthonormal columns of V therefore do not give w-orthogonal v_j. Counterexample: m=2, V=[[1,1],[1,-1]]/sqrt2 gives <(T0+T1),(T0-T1)>_w/2 = pi/4 != 0. The count r_l^0 also mismatches v in R^{r_l}. On a uniform grid the discretized T_k are not orthogonal either, so the abstract's 'orthogonal algebraic Tucker tensor' is likewise unsupported.

failure_location.quote: If \cref{eqn:beta-Tucker} present the orthogonal Tucker tensor, then $\{T_{0:m_\ell-1}(x_\ell)V^{(\ell)}\}$ appear to be the set of $r_\ell^0$ orthogonal polynomials.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the w-orthonormal Chebyshev basis (scale coefficient rows by sqrt(pi), sqrt(pi/2)) before orthonormalizing V, or orthogonalize discretized factors by QR; or drop the claim.
issues.overall_effect: The orthogonality claims for the functional factors and for their grid discretizations are false as stated.
issues.title: Polynomial factors T V are not orthogonal: Chebyshev basis is not orthonormal
issues.why_classification: A routine diagonal rescaling or QR step, or deletion, fixes this side claim. No other result depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We underline that in both cases our Algorithms
Construct the multivariate cubic spline interpolation $Q(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ of the data ${\bf F}$ on the uniform grid

issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims that in the algebraic case too, only (approximate) values at Chebyshev nodes are needed and fine-grid storage is avoided. Algorithm 2 takes the full n1 x n2 x n3 tensor F as input and builds a global trivariate spline from all of its entries. The claim holds only for the functional and CP-input variants.

failure_location.quote: but does not require storage of the discretized function on the fine 3D-grid

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the mesh-free claim to Algorithms 1, 3 and 4, and state that Algorithm 2 requires full-grid data.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised mesh-free property, and the abstract's coverage of functions 'only available on a regular grid', fail for full-tensor input.
issues.title: Mesh-free claim false for full-tensor algebraic case (Algorithm 2)
issues.why_classification: An advertised property is withdrawn for one input class, though the main CP-input algorithm keeps it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $C_6 nR + C_7 mR + C_9 m R\log m + C_{10} mR \min\{m,R\} + C_{11} R |\log \varepsilon|^3$

issues.failure_explanation: Algorithm 4 needs O(nR) for the splines, O(mR log m) for the DCTs, O(mR min{m,R}) for the side-matrix SVDs and O(R r^3) for the core. Prop. compl states exactly this, which is not O(mR) (note n >> m).

failure_location.quote: the memory and computational cost are both $\mathcal{O}(mR)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace O(mR) with the bound of prop:compl.
issues.overall_effect: The stated computational cost of the preferred algorithm is understated.
issues.title: O(mR) cost claim for Algorithm 4 contradicts its own complexity bound
issues.why_classification: A local wording correction suffices, and the algorithm's preference still holds.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The desired result then follows from the standard error analysis of the RHOSVD truncation

issues.failure_explanation: The cited RHOSVD bound (||xi|| times tail singular values of side matrices) is for CP tensors with normalized canonical vectors. The vectors c_k = W q_k of C are not normalized, yet the bound uses the weights xi of F, and sigma_k^(l) is never defined. The stated RHS is not invariant under the rescaling xi_k -> xi_k/s^3, c_k -> s c_k, which leaves C unchanged but scales the RHS by s^{-2}. So it cannot hold in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize c_k^(l), set xi~_k = xi_k prod_l ||c_k^(l)||, define sigma_k^(l) as singular values of the normalized side matrices, and restate the lemma and theorem with ||xi~||.
issues.overall_effect: The RHOSVD part of the error bound in Lemma ftilde-fhat and Theorem added-1, and the adaptive rank selection based on it, are unreliable as stated.
issues.title: RHOSVD error bound applied to unnormalized canonical vectors; sigma undefined
issues.why_classification: A routine renormalization keeps the bound's form, computability and use.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $C_4 m^3(m+n) + C_5 m^3 + C_1 m^3 \log m + C_2 m^4 + C_3 m^4 |\log \varepsilon|$

issues.failure_explanation: The trivariate cubic spline interpolates all n^3 entries of F, and its coefficients depend globally on them. Any construction therefore costs Omega(n^3); mode-wise evaluation gives O(n^3 + n^2 m + n m^2 + m^3). The claimed O(m^3(m+n)) is below this lower bound when n is large relative to m^{3/2} (e.g. m=129, n=4096). The 'Similarly' step gives no derivation.

failure_location.quote: Similarly, the cost of trivariate cubic spline interpolation which is required in \cref{alg:cheb_tuck_alg} is $\mathcal{O}(m^3(m+n))$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term with O(n^3 + n^2 m + n m^2 + m^3), from mode-by-mode 1D spline construction and evaluation.
issues.overall_effect: The complexity guarantee for Algorithm 2 is false in the large-n regime; its true cost scales cubically in n.
issues.title: Algorithm 2 complexity omits the Omega(n^3) cost of processing full-grid data
issues.why_classification: The corrected bound is routine to derive but materially worse (cubic in n) for one advertised algorithm. The main CP-input algorithms are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This assumption is true for a wide range of functions including Newton kernel in our numerical experiments

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition states the |log eps| and |log eps|^3 terms unconditionally for arbitrary f or CP input. The proof needs the unproved rank hypothesis r = O(|log eps|). In general r can reach m: the paper's own table shows r = m for m = 9, 17. This would turn the Tucker-ALS term into O(m^5) and the core term into O(R r^3).

failure_location.quote: where the Tucker rank $r = \mathcal{O}(|\log \varepsilon|)$ is assumed

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the bounds in terms of r (e.g. C_3 m^4 r, C_11 R r^3), or add r = O(|log eps|) as an explicit hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The stated complexities for Algorithms 1-4 are valid only under an unstated hypothesis on the Tucker ranks.
issues.title: Complexity bounds rely on unstated assumption r = O(|log eps|)
issues.why_classification: Adding the hypothesis or expressing the bounds in r is a local change that keeps the method and its scope.
